official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 NPS status
official_measurement_examples.fact: Updated EN-1 and EN-5 national policy statements came into force on 6 January 2026 for nationally significant energy and electricity-network infrastructure.

official_measurement_examples.name: Queue scale
official_measurement_examples.fact: NESO reports the connections queue at over 738 GW, far above the clean-generation capacity required by 2030, so queue presence alone is not evidence of near-term deliverability.

official_measurement_examples.name: Demand reform challenge
official_measurement_examples.fact: Ofgem's June 2026 update says the demand queue is large and contains non-viable projects as well as progressed projects delayed by network or generation build.

official_measurement_examples.name: Gate 2 reform
official_measurement_examples.fact: Connections reform prioritises projects under revised readiness and strategic-alignment rules rather than treating every historic queue entry equally.

official_measurement_examples.name: Offer timeline
official_measurement_examples.fact: NESO's February 2026 timeline shows different offer windows extending into 2027 for different Gate 2 phases and connection types.

official_measurement_examples.name: Offer transparency
official_measurement_examples.fact: NESO reported in April 2026 that around 88% of the first tranche of protected Gate 2 offers had been issued, which is programme progress rather than parcel-specific network capacity.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Electricity connection offers, network reinforcement, planning consent and land rights are separate dependencies.

official_measurement_examples.name: Strategic plan limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: National energy plans identify strategic network need but do not prove a particular development parcel has an available connection point, capacity or connection date.

core_rules: national electricity NPS is not a parcel connection offer
grid queue entry is not proof of available capacity
connection offer is not planning permission
planning permission is not an electricity connection offer
Gate 2 status must retain phase and date
queue reform status must not be inferred from old queue position
strategic capacity ranges are not parcel-level capacity
network reinforcement plans do not create land rights
connection timing is not guaranteed by programme-level timelines
transmission and distribution connection routes must not be merged
protected-offer statistics are not site-specific evidence
connection agreement does not prove all reinforcement is complete
electricity network evidence does not determine land ownership
grid strategy does not reserve development capacity on a parcel
no parcel grid-capacity clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official DESNZ, Ofgem, NESO and GOV.UK sources checked on 2026-07-26; 2026 NPS, connections-reform status, queue scale and offer timelines kept as programme evidence rather than parcel capacity.
